video.agency.evidence: [影魔·codex] 我需要持续主动压制冲来的敌人。图1第2行第2–8格（2.25–3.75秒）、第3行（4.00–5.75秒）及第4行第1–4格（6.00–6.75秒），我的双臂基本保持抬起、向外伸展的姿势；黑柱虽有变化，但看不清每发重新垂爪、上捞并举过头顶的主动施法。无法确认我在连续应对敌人，而非保持姿势等待特效自行推进；对应规格1.8–6.6秒九次主动出手，按拿不准判fail。；[树人·claude] From the 0.000–2.000 cells, the near treant groups do charge left toward him, and in the 2.250–3.000 cells the group under the first black column raises its arms, which reads as a reaction to the hit. From 3.500 to 7.750, though, the back waves on the right side of each cell look like a dense, nearly static row that stays far away. Compared with the 4.000, 5.000 and 6.000 cells, this crowd does not clearly move forward. The spec's survival reactions are not visible either: no checking stride, no scattering to the sides, no crouching to sprint, no going around the corpse piles. The spec's beats at 3.3–5.1 s and 5.1–6.9 s call for treants to 'charge through the corpse pile into range at full speed'. Instead they look like they are queuing up to die or waiting in place. The smoke and the small thumbnail also make it impossible to confirm that each column kills one group of treants that falls on its back.

video.readability.evidence: [audience·claude] Watching as a first-time viewer, I can roughly follow the target and the result, but I can't say for sure who cast the skill. Target: a group of small humanoid monsters in the midground on the right (0.0–2.0s). At 2.25s a black smoke tornado suddenly drops among them. Between 2.5 and 3.75s it sweeps them up and they disappear into the smoke. From 4.0 to 8.75s the black pillar keeps swirling in the middle of the frame, and the shapes of the monsters inside it are blurry. Result: from 9.0 to 9.75s the smoke clears and only a few white remains, possibly bones, are left on the ground. Those remains are tiny in the frame and hard to read; you have to guess they mean the monsters died. Caster: the flame giant on the left only raises its arm slightly at about 1.5–2.0s. No projectile, beam or trail of light goes from it to the tornado. The tornado is black smoke, which doesn't match the giant's fire and lava look. From 2.25s on, the giant is cut off by the left edge of the frame, and it is visually separate from the tornado. So a viewer can't tell for sure that the giant cast it; it could just as easily be read as a natural disaster or a third party's skill. Spectacle: the whole effect is grey-black smoke from start to finish and doesn't look very impressive. The caster link and the readability of the result are both unclear, so this check fails.
